swallowed.finding: only liveness arm is namespace import; no named/dynamic arm, no same-file use, and no namespace-site dot/index/destructure spelling

chains.finding: dead declaration with one or more declaration-granular consumers, all themselves dead; reported through fixpoint to head/cycle
chains.caveat: name-based in-file attribution errs alive; unseen DB/proxy/template dispatch can false-positive and amplify

rot.finding: exact shared collectors for unsuppressed orphans, ordinary testonly hits, chains, non-exempt non-union typeonly hits, non-exempt swallowed hits
rot.omissions: does not reproduce standalone marker-staleness and named bucket narration

swallowed: named import and same-file uses excluded
chains: edge map opt-in leaves all liveness sets identical
rot: each section equality-compared to its standalone collector on planted fixture

report.task: Adjudicate completed partial-semantic rot outputs for db, inference, default-content, and showcase-plugins

included: their direct callers, package barrels, tests, and framework/tooling entrypoints
excluded: kit and contracts rot outputs because those runs predated or overlapped candidate repair

method.sourceReading: Read each candidate declaration, its package barrel, relevant callers, and the package headers that state intended ownership. Read the provider-row persistence writer in full to distinguish a truly live schema value from a documented but currently unconsumed export.

structuralSearch.note: A bare identifier pattern does not match a TypeScript type-alias declaration reliably, so the aliases were also searched using explicit type-alias patterns. The explicit patterns found each declaration and no member access for either DB candidate.

textualCorroboration.scope: repository-wide tracked source-oriented glob set, primarily **/*.ts and **/*.tsx; package-name searches also included package.json and docs only to identify declared entrypoint roles
textualCorroboration.result: Corroborated all direct identifier references and package consumers. No candidate was approved for deletion, so there is no deletion claim resting on a negative textual result.

summary.disposition: Keep all six candidates. The scan found no conclusive architecture-neutral deletion. The two packages with zero candidates are live runtime content packages, not deletion candidates.

findings.reason: The DB reset forecast is dynamically imported and invoked by the db-baseline-parity verification operation. That is a live framework/tooling entrypoint outside product runtime, and the integration tests additionally exercise every forecast arm. Calling it test-only loses its actual non-test consumer.
evidence: packages/db/src/client/index.ts:637-661 declares and implements the forecast
packages/db/src/index.ts:24 re-exports it from @orb/db
tooling/src/verify/ops/db-baseline-parity.ts:156-175 dynamically imports and invokes it
tests/db/client.int.test.ts:436-610 covers no-db, trivial, current, unknown, and divergent behavior
ast-grep scanned 6526 TS and 1469 TSX files; it found the tooling calls, DB declaration/barrel, and test references

findings.reason: No direct consumer uses the alias today, but it is the schema type twin derived from the live PROVIDER_ROW_ORIGINS tuple. The tuple itself drives the origin_kind Drizzle enum and SQL CHECK. The task explicitly requires preserving schema/type twins. The swallowed result comes from the complete schema barrel being imported as a namespace by the DB client; it is not evidence that this erased type executes at runtime.

packages/db/src/schema/connection-bindings.ts:109 and :127 consume PROVIDER_ROW_ORIGINS in the live table definition

packages/db/src/client/index.ts:21 imports the schema namespace for Drizzle and typeof schema
explicit ast-grep type-alias search found the declaration; member-access searches found no direct ProviderRowOrigin consumer across 6526 TS files
repository-wide rg over TS/TSX found only the declaration

findings.reason: The export has no direct caller. Its declaration explicitly names it as the closed task tuple for validating provider_rows.serves on write, but the current writer accepts an already validated ProviderDef and writes row.serves directly; the contract schema is the present validation authority. This is intended validation surface that is presently unwired, not proven superseded residue. Preserve the explicit seam and route any decision to remove or wire it through the provider-row design owner.
evidence: packages/db/src/schema/connection-bindings.ts:136-137 states the validation-seam intent and derives the value from canonical TASKS
packages/server/src/domain/connection/persistence/provider-rows.ts:1-4 states that providerDefSchema validates the JSON arrays on write
packages/server/src/domain/connection/persistence/provider-rows.ts:35-58 writes row.serves without consuming PROVIDER_ROW_TASKS

repository-wide rg over TS/TSX found only the declaration
findings.followUp: Architectural/product decision only: either wire this exported tuple into a DB-owned validation boundary or explicitly retire the claimed seam. Do not delete it as incidental rot.

It is re-exported from the inference contract barrel. This is exactly the repository's unwired-intent case and must not be treated as deletion evidence.

It is deliberately exported through the local-light and package barrels and is consumed by inference, server boot, and embeddings tests to select the same production seed row and verify model-space agreement. It is a stable test-facing seam, not product runtime code and not dead residue.

durableLesson.title: Namespace-swallowed rot candidates need symbol-kind adjudication
durableLesson.hook: A complete schema namespace makes values look consumed and can make erased type exports look swallowed; inspect direct member accesses, schema/type-twin intent, and the barrel contract before deleting.
durableLesson.body: For DB schema rot, the namespace import into Drizzle is required for table reachability but is a conservative liveness sink. A swallowed candidate may be a live table value, an erased type twin, or a documented future seam. Search the exact member access structurally in both TS and TSX, corroborate textually, then read the declaration and the actual writer before assigning deletion.

summary.conclusion: No deletion is justified. The three orphan exports are intentional package API surfaces with explicit anatomy or generated-map provenance. The 43 test-only exports divide into 37 public component/framework entrypoints and six proof-facing exports, one of which also has live runtime consumers. The rot lens is accurate as a candidate generator; treating candidate status as deletion authority would produce 46 false-positive deletions.

false_positives.explanation: No candidate is falsely labeled under the lens's narrow meanings of orphan-export or test-only-export. Every label matches the semantic graph inspected. All 46 are non-actionable for deletion because package entrypoints and proof seams are deliberately retained contracts.
